_meta.indication: RUKOBIA, in combination with other antiretroviral(s), is indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1 infection failing their current antiretroviral regimen due to resistance, intolerance, or safety considerations.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, partially-randomized, international, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. For the first 8 days subjects in the randomized cohort received FTR 600 mg BID or placebo added to their failing regimen (blinded functional monotherapy); after Day 8 all received open-label FTR 600 mg BID plus optimized background therapy (OBT) for at least 96 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Heavily treatment-experienced (HTE) adults with multidrug-resistant (MDR) HIV-1 infection failing their current antiretroviral regimen due to resistance, intolerance, or safety considerations.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: change in HIV-1 RNA log10 copies/mL from Day 1 to Day 8.
pivotal_trials.n: Randomized cohort N=272 (203 FTR, 69 placebo); plus non-randomized cohort N=99.
pivotal_trials.result: Primary endpoint: adjusted mean change in HIV-1 RNA Day 1 to Day 8 was -0.791 for RUKOBIA vs -0.166 for placebo; adjusted mean difference -0.625 (95% CI -0.810, -0.441), demonstrating superiority. At Day 8, 65% (131/203) of RUKOBIA subjects vs 19% (13/69) placebo achieved >0.5 log10 decline. HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL was achieved in 53% at Week 24 and 60% at Week 96.

key_safety: Most adverse reactions were mild or moderate (81%); 7% discontinued due to an AE at Week 96. The most common adverse reaction (≥5%) was nausea (10%); other reactions in the randomized cohort included diarrhea (4%), headache (4%), abdominal pain (3%), dyspepsia (3%), fatigue (3%), rash (3%), sleep disturbance (3%), immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (2%), somnolence (2%), and vomiting (2%). Warnings include immune reconstitution syndrome, QTc prolongation at higher-than-recommended doses, and elevations in hepatic transaminases in patients with HBV/HCV co-infection.
target_moa: Fostemsavir is a prodrug hydrolyzed to the active moiety temsavir, an HIV-1 attachment inhibitor. Temsavir binds directly to the gp120 subunit within the HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein gp160, selectively inhibiting the interaction between the virus and CD4 receptors and thereby preventing attachment and viral entry into host cells.
modality: Small molecule (first-in-class HIV-1 gp120-directed attachment inhibitor; prodrug of temsavir).

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues unexpected in the intended population.

summary.text: RUKOBIA (fostemsavir), a first-in-class HIV-1 gp120-directed attachment inhibitor, received Fast Track Designation (February 16, 2011) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (June 24, 2015), and the NDA was granted Priority review. It was approved on standard (full) approval based on the Phase 3 BRIGHTE trial, without accelerated approval; the application was not referred to an advisory committee.
